name: quake
title: QUAKE (WinQuake, id386=0)
_host: Which shell branch presents this build. It belongs to the VARIANT, not to the target: one engine, four platform layers, and the page has to know which one it is looking at. Node needs none of this -- `targets/quake.json:x11` has always been enough there -- which is why it was missing.
_units: The engine, shared by both platforms. id386=0 is a BUILD OPTION of Quake's own, not a modification: the source ships a C equivalent of every .s file and the makefile picks one.
_defines: __i386__ and i386 are UNDEFINED on purpose. PRISM's target macros set them because the target IS i386, but Quake reads them as 'the x86 assembly is available', which is the opposite of id386=0.
_inline: quakedef.h declares isDedicated and every real platform's sys_*.c defines it -- except sys_null.c, the one id ships for exactly this situation. So it falls to whoever supplies the platform.

null._web: NODE ONLY, and it earns that: this is the porting-stub build, whose Sys_FloatTime returns `t += 0.1` -- a counter, not a clock. Anything it measures about ITSELF is fiction, which makes it a fine compile test and a bad thing to hand somebody as a playable Quake. The page offers the three real platforms.
null._doc: The porting stub set Quake ships for exactly this situation: no real input, sound or timing. Sys_FloatTime here returns t += 0.1 -- a counter, not a clock -- so anything this build measures about ITSELF is fiction, and only a wall clock outside it means anything.

win.title: QUAKE (Win32, id386=0)
win._doc: The Windows client, from WinQuake.dsp's own source list minus the twelve gl_* units of the GLQuake configuration. The platform set is the difference between that and the shared engine list: cd_win.c conproc.c in_win.c net_win.c net_wins.c net_wipx.c snd_dma.c snd_mem.c snd_mix.c snd_win.c sys_win.c vid_win.c.
win._generated: What the ASSEMBLER provides in a real build. sys_wina.s exports five routines and sys_win.c already defines four of them in C, so this is the DOS file minus what WinQuake writes itself -- using that one whole reported four duplicate definitions. win32-app.c is the non-graphical half of the Win32 shim -- last-error, code pages, module handles -- and win32.c is the window. Six functions moved from the second to the first when PuTTY needed them without a window; anything including win32.c includes win32-app.c.
win._include: The DirectX and SciTech MGL headers SHIP WITH THE SOURCE, so nothing here has to invent them -- only MGLLT.LIB is binary, which makes the MGL calls undefined symbols rather than parse errors. Exactly MAME's relationship with Allegro.
win._net: net_none.c instead of net_win.c + net_wins.c + net_wipx.c, the substitution the DOS and X11 variants already make. Winsock is a surface of its own and is not the point of this target.

x11.title: QUAKE (Linux/X11, id386=0)
x11._doc: The Linux/X11 client -- `quake.x11` in the game's own Makefile.linuxi386. The platform units are the difference between that makefile's X11_OBJS and the shared engine list above, computed rather than chosen: net_udp.c net_bsd.c cd_linux.c sys_linux.c vid_x.c snd_dma.c snd_mem.c snd_mix.c snd_linux.c. Its 18 assembly objects are the id386=1 build and are exactly what the C files already listed replace.
x11._cd: cd_null.c rather than the shipped cd_linux.c. That file wants a real linux/cdrom.h -- five structs and thirteen ioctl numbers -- and would buy a CD player for a machine with no CD drive. cd_null.c is Quake's own file for this situation and Makefile.linuxi386 links it for its own targets, so this is a build selection, not a modification.
x11._net: net_udp.c and net_bsd.c are the shipped pair and want BSD sockets, which PRISM does not have. net_none.c is the same substitution the DOS variant already makes, and it is a build option of Quake's own -- Makefile.linuxi386 links net_none.o for the dedicated server. The socket surface is 8 functions and is recorded rather than worked around.

dos._args: -nosound, and ONLY that. snd_dos.c drives a Gravis Ultrasound or a Sound Blaster through ports nothing here answers, so without the switch the game reaches GUS_Init and stops -- the program's own option for a machine with no sound card. `-mem 16` used to be here too and should not have been: the game sizes its heap by walking sbrk down in 64K steps until one succeeds, PRISM's sbrk refused every size, and the loop ran the value negative. That was a bug in the runtime, not a preference of this build (see src/runtime/runtime.js).
dos._doc: The units the game actually shipped with. NOT a one-for-one swap: snd_null.c also DEFINES the sound cvars and shm, which the engine and the menu reference, so dropping it means picking up Quake's real sound core as well as its DOS driver. The null build was missing a third of the program, not just its output stage.
dos._generated: What the LINKER and the ASSEMBLER provide in a real DJGPP build: start_of_memory, the x87 control-word routines, and VGA_UpdateLinearScreen transcribed from d_copy.s.
dos._env: Three devices and a clock. Mode 13h needs none of them: it is a linear framebuffer at 0xA0000, which PRISM already has because the low megabyte is reserved.

svgalib.title: QUAKE (Linux svgalib, id386=0)
svgalib._doc: id's OTHER Linux video driver: vid_svgalib.c draws to the virtual console's framebuffer with no X server at all, and reads the RAW keyboard. It is a whole platform layer in one file -- VID_*, Sys_SendKeyEvents and every IN_* -- like vid_x.c and vid_sunx.c, so this is a second display path on the same MACHINE rather than a new machine.
svgalib._planar: The driver has a planar path (`if (VGA_planar) VGA_UpdatePlanarScreen(...)`, the routine that blocks P3.5) and never takes it here, for a reason rather than by luck: `VGA_planar = modes[current_mode].bytesperpixel == 0` and with no arguments it selects G320x200x256, which on a real svgalib is a LINEAR eight-bit mode. Ask for a planar mode and it would need the same two things mode-X needs.
svgalib._snd: snd_null.c rather than snd_linux.c: /dev/dsp is a separate device surface and not what this variant is for. The X11 variant is where the sound path is exercised.

sun.title: QUAKE (SunOS/X11, id386=0)
sun._args: Not tuning. vid_sunx.c takes its framebuffer from Quake's ZONE with Z_Malloc where vid_x.c uses malloc, and the zone's default 0xc000 is 49,152 bytes against a 320x200 frame's 64,000. This build cannot start without it on any machine, so it belongs to the variant rather than to whoever types the command line.
sun._doc: id shipped a SUN platform layer and nobody has ever built it here: sys_sun.c, in_sun.c, snd_sun.c and TWO video drivers -- vid_sunx.c over plain Xlib and vid_sunxil.c over Sun's XIL imaging library. The XIL one needs a proprietary library that does not exist outside SunOS; the Xlib one needs exactly the Xlib PRISM already shims for Doom, which is why this variant is worth having: a FOURTH platform layer over the same renderer, and the cheapest new axis the corpus offers.
sun._snd: snd_null.c rather than the shipped snd_sun.c: that file opens /dev/audio and drives Sun's own audio ioctls, which is a device surface of its own and not what this variant is for. The same substitution the DOS variant makes for its Gravis card.
sun._net: net_none.c, as x11 and dos already do.
sun._in: in_sun.c is NOT built, and that is a selection id's own tree offers: vid_sunx.c defines IN_Init, IN_Shutdown, IN_Commands and IN_Move itself -- exactly as vid_x.c does for the Linux build -- while in_sun.c is the fuller alternative, reaching for gethrtime and XChangePointerControl. Building both defines each of the four twice.

glx.title: GLQUAKE (Linux/GLX, id386=0)
glx._doc: glquake.glx in the game's own Makefile.linuxi386: GLQUAKE_OBJS plus GLX_OBJS (gl_vidlinuxglx.c), compiled with GLCFLAGS' -DGLQUAKE. The same substitutions as the x11 variant, for the same reasons: cd_null.c for cd_linux.c and net_none.c for net_udp.c/net_bsd.c. The four .s objects are the id386=1 build; with id386=0 the C files listed already carry their equivalents. OpenGL is src/env/gl.js; GLX is the glx environment beside the X11 shim.

wgl.title: GLQUAKE (Win32, opengl32, id386=0)
wgl._doc: glquake.exe: WinQuake.dsp's GL configuration (/D GLQUAKE), which compiles the twelve gl_* units instead of the software renderer and vid_win.c. So it is the GLX variant's engine list with its four Linux platform files (sys_linux, snd_linux, cd_null, gl_vidlinuxglx) swapped for the Win32 ones the win variant already uses, and gl_vidnt.c -- which links opengl32 directly, calling wgl* and gl* by name, and with no texture-object extension advertised takes glBindTexture from LoadLibrary("opengl32.dll")/GetProcAddress. opengl32.dll is src/env/opengl32.c over src/env/gl.js. net_none.c as in the win variant.
wgl._generated: The win variant's Win32 shim without mgl.c, which is the software renderer's display boundary; the GL build draws through WGL instead.
wgl._args: -window: gl_vidnt.c otherwise asks ChangeDisplaySettings for a fullscreen mode, which the page refuses (it cannot change a display mode), and the windowed mode is the one id offers for that case.
